findings.title: 'Carried by a gate that can refuse' over-credits rules whose obligation is model-carried
findings.detail: The 16-rule 'gate' class is defined as 'a validator, hook or test blocks the forbidden outcome', but classification follows the presence of an enforced_by entry, not what it blocks. git-history-discipline is counted as gated, yet its own text says the guard only blocks --no-verify/hooksPath overrides, and only on claude. Unsolicited rebase, squash and amend are not blocked. language-and-tone (a markdown-language validator) and secret-vcs-guard (a CI scan, not the agent-side write gate) have the same problem. The 16/10/15/80 split therefore overstates mechanical coverage, and the report itself warns against exactly this inflation.
findings.rationale: Each non-kernel rule with a law section now declares stable obligation ids (src/config/rule-obligations.json) and an enforced_by entry binds only to the ids its gate actually refuses; check_enforcement_coverage prints the narrower obligation count beside the unchanged rule count. The three named rules are no longer counted whole: git-history-discipline is credited with 1 of 4 obligations (no-hook-bypass only — rebase/squash/amend/drop stay unbound), secret-vcs-guard with 1 of 4 (no-credential-in-tracked-file), and language-and-tone is a kernel rule reported at its own rule-granularity cohort rather than folded into the per-obligation count. The rule-level figure this finding quoted is unchanged by design (D3) and still prints first; the obligation figure beside it is the corrected reading.

findings.title: Workspace literal scope entries follow symlinks out of the project root
findings.detail: In the reviewed runner.ts, _behavior_scopes rejects `..`, absolute paths and `!` globs. For a literal workspace entry it uses fs.statSync(...).isDirectory(), which follows symlinks. A workspace entry naming an in-repo symlink to a directory outside the root is accepted as a scope. Detection then reads composer.json, package.json and similar files outside the repository. The glob branch uses Dirent.isDirectory(), which does not follow symlinks, so the two branches are inconsistent. Impact is limited to detection output in a local resolver, but the module's own comments claim path confinement. Use lstatSync, or realpath-confine the result.
findings.rationale: Carried by road-to-the-16-3-0-findings-residue (item 1). findings.title: pnpm-workspace parser drops all scopes on CRLF files

findings.title: Workspace scope expansion follows symlinks for literal entries and reads files outside the project root
findings.detail: _behavior_scopes accepts a literal workspace entry after fs.statSync(path.join(project_root, g)).isDirectory(). statSync follows symlinks, so a literal entry that is a symlink to a directory outside the repository becomes a scope. Detection then reads composer.json, package.json, requirements.txt, Gemfile and .NET project files there. The '..' and leading-'/' guards do not cover a symlink inside the tree. The glob branch uses Dirent.isDirectory(), which does not follow symlinks, so the two branches disagree. Impact is low: the code only pattern-matches the content, and basis strings echo file names, not content. Still, an untrusted repository can steer the resolver to read arbitrary local manifests. Use lstat or a realpath containment check for the literal branch.
findings.rationale: Carried by road-to-the-16-3-0-findings-residue (item 1). The vector the finding names (a literal entry that is a symlink to an outside directory, accepted through statSync) is closed by the lstatSync check in the literal branch of _behavior_scopes (00612c1f2, #2144, in the 16.3.0 tag), which was the finding's own suggested fix. The outcome it describes is not: lstat resolves only the last segment, so a literal 'pkg/x' whose 'pkg' is a symlink outside the root still reads files outside it, and the glob branch's readdirSync follows a symlinked parent the same way. No test pins the fix. Recorded open because the finding's outcome is still reachable.

findings.title: Review manifest declares a read-only tool set, but the findings cite executed commands
findings.detail: behavior-vocabulary-close-round15.findings.md declares `tools: [git-diff-branch-scoped, file-read-branch-paths]` and `excluded: [..., agents/runtime, ...]`. The prompt template allows only branch-scoped `git diff` and reads of branch-touched files, with no repo-wide grep. The findings table and the 'Verified and NOT findings' block report results that need more than that: `vitest` reporting 119 passed, `lint_roadmap_complexity` exiting 1, `grep -rn 'stack-adaptive' src/ | wc -l` returning 8, a `sha256` of the corpus file, `wc -w` on SKILL.md, and a read of `src/config/canonical-terms.yml`, which is not branch-touched. Either the manifest understates what the reviewer did, or those verifications were not produced by the declared tools. In both cases the recorded provenance of the gate evidence is wrong. The review also records `roadmap: none` and `ac_hash: none`, yet it certifies roadmap and acceptance-criteria claims. Disposition: must-fix. Correct the manifest to the tools actually used, or drop the claims that cannot be reproduced under the stated allowlist.
findings.rationale: Carried by road-to-the-16-3-0-findings-residue. behavior-vocabulary-close-round15.findings.md still declares a read-only tool set while its rows report a vitest run, a lint exit code and a sha256.
